contains: +- Fix: an address such as `me@corp.example@attacker.example` no longer inherits trust from its trusted-looking prefix; look-alike (non-ASCII) characters inside an address are treated as a new value.
+- Fix: arguments a tool spec did not declare (for example a model-invented `bcc`) are now checked for untrusted addresses and links.
+- Fix: guard reasons escape non-ASCII characters, so look-alikes are visible and a narrow Windows console cannot crash on them; the CLI no longer raises on non-ASCII output.
+- Docs: how to declare sinks, tags and risk; what to do with `ask`; a runnable agent loop; a note that hosts are matched by host and path only.
+- Found by a fresh-agent walkthrough of the 0.1.0 README.
+The declarations are the security boundary, so it is worth getting them right. A complete, runnable agent loop is in [`examples/agent_loop.py`](examples/agent_loop.py).

+**Risk** (what the tool can do): `Risk.READ` (reads data), `Risk.WRITE` (a reversible change), `Risk.EXTERNAL` (sends data out or acts irreversibly: email, payment, delete) and `Risk.OUTPUT` (the reply to the user). A tool with no hints is treated as external.
+**Sinks** (parameters that decide where data goes or what an action targets) are declared per parameter with a `SinkSpec(kind, allow_tags=())`:
+| kind | use it for | how the value is matched |
